sections.html:
Norfolk sits in northeastern Nebraska in Madison County, where the North Fork of the Elkhorn River meets the main stem. The 2020 count was 24,955 people in 10,176 households. Of 10,909 housing units, 6.7% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.2%, so houses for sale rarely sit empty for long. The rental vacancy rate was 8.8%, which matters to a landlord thinking about selling a tenant-occupied property.

U.S. Route 81 follows 13th Street on the west side of downtown, U.S. Route 275 crosses the south side on Omaha Avenue, and Nebraska Highway 35 heads northeast toward Wayne. A house near 13th Street or Omaha Avenue is a short drive from most of town, which helps when buyers compare blocks.

Railroads turned a farming settlement into a town. Lines arrived in 1879, 1880 and 1882, Norfolk passed 1,000 residents in 1886, and the population reached 3,883 in 1900, 8,634 in 1920 and 10,717 in 1930. Much of the older housing near the center probably dates from those decades.

Sellers of early twentieth century homes often deal with original wiring, plumbing and foundations. A buyer who finances with a mortgage will want those inspected, and the lender may ask for repairs before it funds the loan. A cash buyer builds those costs into the price instead of asking you to repair them first.

Norfolk is the main retail and service center for the northeast part of the state. Tyson Fresh Meats, Faith Regional Health Services, Northeast Community College, Norfolk Public Schools and Nucor are among the larger employers. A plant shift change, a hospital job offer in another town or a retirement is often the reason a house goes on the market, and a household that must relocate on a deadline tends to value a quick, certain closing over a long listing period.

Expect snowy, cold winters and hot summers. At the airport, normals show about 27 inches of precipitation and nearly 30 inches of snowfall in a typical year. Buyers look first at the roof and gutters, the furnace and insulation, and the air conditioning. If the roof is old or the furnace is near the end of its life, weigh a repair bill against an as-is sale.

The Elkhorn River adds a second question. The 2019 flood damaged the city levees, and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers awarded a $2.69 million contract on April 22, 2020 to repair the Norfolk Elkhorn River levee projects on both banks. If a property is in a mapped flood zone, the lender will require flood insurance and the buyer will ask what it costs. The Nebraska Department of Natural Resources runs the state floodplain program, and the National Weather Service posts live river readings for the Elkhorn at Norfolk.

The most common snag before a sale is a nuisance notice under Chapter 17 of the Norfolk Municipal Code, which covers weeds, litter and vehicles on private property. Clean these up before you sell, or settle them with the buyer in writing, so a closing does not stall.

  • Weeds and noxious growth count as a nuisance once they pass 12 inches in height.
  • Inoperable, wrecked or unregistered vehicles may not stay longer than 30 days unless they are inside an enclosed building.
  • The city serves notice by personal delivery or certified mail. If the owner does not ask for a hearing or comply within five days of receipt, the city can do the work and assess the cost against the lot like a special tax.
  • An administrative fee of $25 is added to weed, litter and drainage billings.

Permits follow the fee schedule in Section 2-5 of the code. As of the October 2025 update, new construction and additions cost $0.26 per finished square foot above grade and $0.18 per square foot for basements. A basement finish or remodel is $0.215 per square foot, the minimum permit is $36.25 and a demolition permit is $54. Starting work before you apply triples the permit fee.

A basement finished without a permit is likely to draw questions during the buyer's inspection. Mention it before they find it, and let them decide how to proceed.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Madison County
sections.html:
The Madison County Register of Deeds records a Norfolk sale. Send the deed along with a Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, which comes from the Nebraska Department of Revenue.

Document lengthRecording fee
One page$10
Two pages$16
Three pages$22
Each added page$6

The larger cost is the state documentary stamp tax. Whoever signs the deed as grantor pays $3.32 per $1,000 of value (any fraction counts) on deeds recorded July 18, 2026 or later. Certain transfers escape it, so look at the department's exemption list when a deed passes between relatives or out of an estate.

Madison County bills real and personal property tax due December 31. May 1 of the following year is the delinquency date for the first half, and September 1 for the second. Overdue amounts to political subdivisions accrue interest at 14 percent a year under Nebraska law. The title company usually divides the current year's tax between the two sides at closing, so get the number before you sign.

An inherited house may need to pass through county court probate before anyone can sign a deed. A rental needs its lease terms reviewed. A house carrying a nuisance notice needs the weeds, vehicles or litter cleared, or the issue handed to the buyer in writing.

Paying cash removes the lender, so an appraisal and loan approval stop controlling your closing date. You still sign a deed, the Madison County recording steps still apply, and a title company still checks that taxes and liens are cleared. To compare routes, request a written offer and set it beside a list-and-repair plan with your own figures. Hearing a cash offer costs you nothing.

sections.h2: Preparing a Norfolk house for sale
sections.html:
A few hours of homework before you talk to buyers can save a closing. Walk the lot for weeds above 12 inches and for any vehicle that has sat unmoved for more than 30 days. Look at the roof and gutters after the last winter, and note the age of the furnace. Pull any permit records you have, especially for a finished basement or an addition. Then ask the Treasurer for a balance and, if the house came to you through an estate, ask the title company what court papers it needs.

None of this requires spending money. It just means the buyer hears about problems from you, in writing, rather than discovering them at the inspection.

Owners near the Elkhorn should also dig out any flood insurance paperwork, since a buyer's lender may ask for it first.

faqs.q: How much is the Nebraska deed tax on a Norfolk house?
faqs.a: The charge is $3.32 per $1,000 of value on deeds recorded July 18, 2026 or later, unless an exemption applies. The Register of Deeds collects it at recording.

faqs.q: When are Madison County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due December 31. The first half is late after the following May 1 and the second half after September 1, and late amounts carry 14 percent annual interest. Ask the Madison County Treasurer for balances before closing.

faqs.q: Can the city of Norfolk bill me for yard or vehicle problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Chapter 17 of the municipal code, if you do not request a hearing or fix a nuisance within five days of receiving notice, the city can abate it and assess the cost against the property like a special tax. Weeds over 12 inches and vehicles inoperable for more than 30 days are covered.

faqs.q: Does Norfolk have flood risk that affects a sale?
faqs.a: Parts of the city sit along the Elkhorn River. Its 2019 flood damaged levees and led to a $2.69 million Army Corps repair contract. In a mapped flood zone, a lender may demand flood insurance, so look up the flood map for your address early.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Madison County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $10 for one page, $16 for two and $22 for three, plus $6 for each added page. The deed also needs a Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521.
